land.text: Ijebu, the southern edge of the Ife empire ('Ijebu in the south')

predecessors.note: The Ife Empire infobox lists the Ijebu Kingdom among its successors without a date; the Ijebu page says only 'formed around the 15th century'. 1420 is the Ife dossier's end.

land.text: Ijebu, after the 1892 war ('annexed to the colony of Southern Nigeria', undated)

successors.note: The Ijebu page and the Ijebu Ode page give no year for the annexation; the Lagos Colony page has the colony's protectorate over most of Yorubaland between 1890 and 1897; the Southern Nigeria Protectorate (niger-coast-protectorate) took the Lagos protectorate on 28 February 1906.

capitals.name: Ijebu Ode
capitals.note: 'The capital is at Ijebu Ode where the Awujale has his palace'; coordinates 6.82083 N, 3.92083 E on the Ijebu Ode page; 'by the 16th century, it was established as the chief town'.

correction.text: the Ijebu kingdom round Ijebu Ode, ruled by the Awujale

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'It was formed around the 15th century'; 'The state rose in power in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries'; the infobox map shows the kingdom in c. 1780. Neither page gives an area or a frontier; a 50 km circle round Ijebu Ode (about 8,000 km2) stands for it.

region.text: Ijebu Ode and the Ijebu country

ledger.note: 15th century: the Ijebu kingdom is formed. 'It was formed around the 15th century' under Obanta 'according to legend'; the Ife Empire page lists it among Ife's successors. 1420 is the end of Ife (confidence 1).

region.text: the Ijebu country from Epe to Ijebu Ode

ledger.note: 1892 (12 May): the British land at Epe. 'On 12 May 1892, the captain and his men, including some carriers, sailed up the Lagos Lagoon and landed at Epe' (Ijebu Ode page: the 1892 Ijebu Expedition, also the Battle of Imagbon). Ijebu page: 'the British Empire declared war on the Ijebu kingdom in response to its barriers on trade' and 'made efficient use of the Maxim gun'.
1892: Ijebu Ode falls. 'The British emerged victorious in the conflict and captured the Ijebu capital'; the Awujale surrendered 'shortly afterward' (Ijebu Ode page). No month on either page.

1892: Ijebu passes to the British. 'The British emerged victorious ... and captured the Ijebu capital'; 'Ijebu kingdom was later annexed to the colony of southern Nigeria' (Ijebu Ode page), undated; the Lagos Colony page has Lagos making a protectorate over most of Yorubaland 1890-1897 and attacking Ijebu in 1892.
1892: the independent Ijebu Kingdom ends. The Awujale remains as ruler under British protection (the dynasty and office continue to the present, per the Ijebu Ode page).

wars.name: Ijebu Expedition

zones.text: the Ijebu country from Epe to Ijebu Ode

wars.outcome: British victory: landing at Epe 12 May 1892, Ijebu Ode captured, Awujale surrendered 'shortly afterward'; the kingdom annexed (undated) to the colony of Southern Nigeria.
wars.note: The Ijebu page says the British 'declared war ... in response to its barriers on trade'; neither page names the British governor (Carter appears on the Lagos Colony page: 'Carter attacked Ijebu in 1892'); commanders on the Ijebu Ode page: Captain C.M. Denton and Colonel F.C. Scott.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier; the shape is a circle round the capital.

sources.title: Ijebu Kingdom
sources.note: Formed around the 15th century (Obanta); capital Ijebu Ode; Portuguese 1508 and 1620 mentions; war of 1892, Maxim guns, capital captured, annexed (undated) to Southern Nigeria; no area.

sources.title: Ijebu Ode
sources.note: Landing at Epe 12 May 1892; the Awujale surrendered shortly afterward; coordinates 6.82083 N, 3.92083 E; chief town by the 16th century; annexed to Southern Nigeria (undated).

notes: Ijebu has no Cliopatria row. Two pages opened (Ijebu Expedition, Anglo-Ijebu and similar URLs gave URL_NOT_FOUND for 'Ijebu_Expedition'). The founding year is a bridge to Ife's end (1420); the 15th century is all the page says. The pages give no annexation year and no treaty: the dossier ends the independent kingdom in 1892 with the Lagos Colony as successor (protectorate, vassal in the Lagos dossier to 1906). The Ijebu Ode page's 'Awujale surrendered shortly afterward' has no month. Not placed: the Ife/Benin tributary tradition (Ewuare page: Ijebu 'temporarily' under Edo suzerainty, not confirmed by Ijebu tradition), the Egba and Oyo relations (not on the page), Ijebu-Remo and Ijebu-Igbo as sub-kingdoms. No rulers list on the pages (the Awujale's dynasty undated).
